case_name: Rev. Father W. Proost and Others v State of Bihar and Others
petitioner: Rev. Father W. Proost and Others
facts: The Principal and the Rector of St. Xavier's Co,liege, Ranchi and two parents of students have filed the present petition under Art. 32 of the Constitution.
The petition also purports to be filed on behalf of St. Xavier's College, Ranchi and the Association of St. Xavier.
St. Xavier's College was established by the Jesuits of Ranchi.
It was affiliated to Patna University in 1944.
The management of the college vests in a Governing Body consisting of 11 members.
All appointments to the teaching staff, both Religious and Lay are reported to the Syndicate of the Patna University.

The object of rounding the college inter alia is 'to give Catholic youth a full course of moral and liberal education, by imparting a thorough religious instruction and by maintaining a Catholic atmosphere in the institution.'
All non-catholic students receive a course of moral science.
The College was thus rounded by a christian minority and the petitioners claim they have a right to administer it, a constitutional right guaranteed to minorities by Art. 30.

The Bihar Legislature passed an amending Act and introduced in the Bihar Universities Act s. 48-A to come into force from March 1, 1962, which deprives them of this protection and is, therefore, ultra vires.
This provision completely takes away the autonomy of the Governing Body of the College and virtually vests the control of the college in the University Service Commission.
The University began enforcing Art. 178(2) of the New Statutes.

The University asked for an explanation under Art. 179 of the Statutes, how the Governing Body had by-passed the University Service Commission and some teachers were appointed without prior consultation.

Finally the University by a letter, September 26, 1967, communicated to the College that the Senate had decided on September 24, 1967 to withdraw the affiliation of the College u/art. 171 of the Statutes for violating the said provisions of the Act and the Statutes With effect from the session of 1969-70.
While this petition was pending in this Court, the Governor of Bihar promulgated an Ordinance on July 16, 1968.
issues: Whether s. 48-A of the Bihar State Universities (University of Bihar, Bhagalpur and Ranchi) Act, 1960 as amended by Second Amendment Act, 1961 is ultra vires Arts. 29 and 30 of the Constitution.
Whether the University Service Commission has the power to control the appointments of teachers in affiliated colleges not belonging to the State Government.

Whether the Governing Body of an affiliated college established by a minority based on religion or language has the right to make appointments, dismissals, removals, termination of service or reduction in rank of teachers.
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners claim that they have a constitutional right guaranteed to minorities by Art. 30.
They argue that s. 48-A takes away the autonomy of the Governing Body of the College and virtually vests the control of the college in the University Service Commission.
They contend that the University began enforcing Art. 178(2) of the New Statutes without consulting them, which is a violation of their rights.
They argue that the withdrawal of affiliation by the Senate was arbitrary and violative of their fundamental rights.
respondent_arguments: The respondents argue that s. 48-A is a reasonable restriction on the autonomy of the Governing Body of the College to ensure that appointments are made in accordance with the principles of merit and efficiency.
They contend that the University Service Commission has the power to control the appointments of teachers in affiliated colleges not belonging to the State Government.
They argue that the withdrawal of affiliation by the Senate was necessary to maintain the standards of education in the college.
court_reasoning: The Court held that s. 48-A is ultra vires Arts. 29 and 30 of the Constitution because it takes away the autonomy of the Governing Body of the College and virtually vests the control of the college in the University Service Commission.
The Court observed that the University began enforcing Art. 178(2) of the New Statutes without consulting the petitioners, which is a violation of their rights.
The Court held that the withdrawal of affiliation by the Senate was arbitrary and violative of the fundamental rights of the petitioners.
holding: The Supreme Court declared s. 48-A of the Bihar State Universities (University of Bihar, Bhagalpur and Ranchi) Act, 1960 as amended by Second Amendment Act, 1961 ultra vires Arts. 29 and 30 of the Constitution.
The Court ordered that the University Service Commission shall not have any control over the appointments of teachers in affiliated colleges not belonging to the State Government.

The Court held that the Governing Body of an affiliated college established by a minority based on religion or language has the right to make appointments, dismissals, removals, termination of service or reduction in rank of teachers.
cases_cited: On the other hand, in Rev, Sidhaibhai Sabhai and others v. State of Bombay
